newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Bund vols mired as gilts absorb interest.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Bund vols mired as gilts absorb interest.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund options traded on LIFFE moved fractionally higher on Wednesday, but traders said that activity in gilt options is absorbing investors' interest.

Traders said Bund options were relatively quiet, as oscillations in the underlying gilt futures market were distracting investors. Gilt futures traded a record volume on Tuesday after the new chancellor Gordon Brown granted the Bank of England operational independence.
"The range is very narrow in Bunds at the moment," said a broker at a major British brokerage in London.
"It makes a change to have so many enquiries about gilts, and it's to the detriment of Bunds," he said.

Implied volatility of June Bund options rose slightly to 5.0 percent by 1345 GMT compared with 4.98 percent at the open, and was off from about 5.2 percent at the prior close. June Bund futures have traded between 101.71 and 101.85, and were trading down 0.09 at 101.77.

June gilt futures have traded in a range of more than half a point so far this session, and were down 6/32 at 113-07. They posted their biggest one-day gain in five-years on Tuesday, soaring more than two full points.
A trader at a French bank said some upside Bund calls, around the 102.00 strike had traded at a volatility of 4.75 percent. About 3,500 calls had traded at that strike, according to LIFFE data.
Preferred strategy was to buy puts and sell calls as a volatility trade, and hedge against the underlying future.
The spread between gilt and Bund volatility provided an attractive possibility, traders said, but the difference between the bid and ask on volatility quotes made the trade difficult to implement.
"You could fly a jumbo jet through some of the gilt (bid/ask) spreads being quoted," said the British broker, noting that quotes of 7.0 at 7.9 were not uncommon.
He said Bund volatility would remain in the 4.75 to 5.25 percent range until the gilt options market had calmed down next week.
